questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up the price of an item by 40% above the cost price and then offers a discount of 20% on the marked price. What is the shopkeeper's net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price (CP) = ₹100.
Marked Price (MP) = ₹100 + 40% of 100 = ₹140.
Discount = 20% of MP = 0.20 × 140 = ₹28.
Selling Price (SP) = ₹140 − ₹28 = ₹112.
Net Profit = SP − CP = 112 − 100 = 12%.
Hence, Option (B) 12% is correct.

questions.question: Question 6

options.A: tank can be filled by pipe A in 12 hours and by pipe B in 18 hours. Pipe C, when opened alone on a full tank, can empty it in 9 hours. All three pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, and pipe C is closed after 4 hours (A and B continue running). How many additional hours from the moment C is closed will it take to fill the tank completely?

questions.solution:
Q.6 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.6   |  Topic: Quantitative Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:A tank can be filled by pipe A in 12 hours and by pipe B in 18 hours. Pipe C, when opened alone on a full tank, can empty it in 9 hours. All three pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, and pipe C is closed after 4 hours (A and B continue running). How many additional hours from the moment C is closed will it take to fill the tank completely?(A) 5.6 hours(B) 6.0 hours(C) 6.4 hours(D) 7.2 hoursAnswer: (C)Explanation:Rates (tank/hour): A = 1/12, B = 1/18, C = -1/9 (emptying). Combined rate for first 4 hours = 1/12+1/18-1/9 = 3/36+2/36-4/36 = 1/36 per hour. Fraction filled in 4 hours = 4/36 = 1/9. Remaining fraction = 1 - 1/9 = 8/9. After C is closed, combined rate of A and B = 1/12+1/18 = 3/36+2/36 = 5/36 per hour. Time to fill remaining 8/9 = (8/9)/(5/36) = (8/9)x(36/5) = 288/45 = 6.4 hours.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 5.6 hours results from an error in computing the remaining fraction of the tank after the first 4 hours.(B) 6.0 hours results from ignoring the small amount already filled during the first 4 hours and using a slightly wrong combined rate for A and B.(D) 7.2 hours results from using the three-pipe combined rate (1/36) instead of only A and B's rate for the second phase.

questions.question: The average of 11 consecutive odd numbers is 51. If the largest number is increased by 30% and the smallest number is increased by 10% (all other numbers remaining unchanged), what is the new average of all 11 numbers? (Round to one decimal place.)

New average = 583.4/11 = 53.036, which rounds to 53.0.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 51.9 results from increasing only the smallest number and ignoring the change in the largest number.(B) 52.5 results from applying the percentage increases to the average value (51) rather than to the actual largest and smallest numbers.(D) 54.2 results from an error such as increasing both extreme numbers by the same (larger) percentage.

The following is known:(i) T is immediately to the left of P.(ii) S is at one of the two ends of the row.(iii) There are exactly two farms between Q and R.(iv) P is not at either end of the row.(v) Q is to the left of R.(vi) R is immediately adjacent to S.Which farm occupies the middle (3rd) position?(A) Q(B) R(C) S(D) PAnswer: (D)Explanation:Let position(T) = position(P) - 1, from clue (i); position(P) is 2, 3, or 4 from clue (iv). Testing position(P)=3, T=2: clue (ii) requires S at 1 or 5. If S=1, remaining positions {4,5} for Q,R give a gap of only 1, violating clue (iii) (needs gap of 3, i.e. positions differing by 3 with two farms between). If S=5, remaining positions {1,4} for Q,R give |Q-R|=3, satisfying clue (iii); with clue (v) Q is left of R, so Q=1, R=4. Clue (vi) requires R adjacent to S: R=4, S=5 -- adjacent, satisfied. This gives the unique arrangement: Q(1)-T(2)-P(3)-R(4)-S(5). (Testing P=4 similarly yields a candidate arrangement, but clue (vi) — R adjacent to S — eliminates it, since in that case R and S are not adjacent.) Hence the farm in the middle (3rd) position is P.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) Q occupies position 1, not the middle position, in the unique valid arrangement.(B) R occupies position 4, not the middle position.(C) S occupies position 5 (an end), not the middle position.

questions.question: Question 10

options.A: square sheet of paper is folded in half along a vertical line and then folded again in half along a horizontal line, producing a smaller square exactly one-quarter the area of the original sheet, with the folded corner of the small square located at the centre of the original sheet. A hole is punched exactly through the centre of this twice-folded small square, through all layers. When the sheet is fully unfolded, how many holes appear, and how are they arranged? [Figure description: original square sheet, first fold brings the right half onto the left half (vertical crease down the middle), second fold brings the bottom half of the resulting rectangle onto the top half (horizontal crease), yielding a quarter-size square whose folded corner coincides with the centre of the original sheet.]
options.B: 2 holes, symmetric about the vertical fold line only
options.C: 4 holes, one in the centre of each quadrant, symmetric about both the vertical and horizontal centre lines
options.D: 4 holes, all clustered near one corner of the sheet

questions.solution:
Q.10 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Spatial Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.10   |  Topic: Spatial Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:A square sheet of paper is folded in half along a vertical line and then folded again in half along a horizontal line, producing a smaller square exactly one-quarter the area of the original sheet, with the folded corner of the small square located at the centre of the original sheet. A hole is punched exactly through the centre of this twice-folded small square, through all layers. When the sheet is fully unfolded, how many holes appear, and how are they arranged? [Figure description: original square sheet, first fold brings the right half onto the left half (vertical crease down the middle), second fold brings the bottom half of the resulting rectangle onto the top half (horizontal crease), yielding a quarter-size square whose folded corner coincides with the centre of the original sheet.](A) 1 hole, at the exact centre of the sheet(B) 2 holes, symmetric about the vertical fold line only(C) 4 holes, one in the centre of each quadrant, symmetric about both the vertical and horizontal centre lines(D) 4 holes, all clustered near one corner of the sheetAnswer: (C)Explanation:The corner of the twice-folded quarter-square that is shared by both fold creases corresponds to the centre of the original sheet. The hole is punched at the centre of the folded quarter-square, i.e. at a point offset equally from both fold lines. Unfolding the horizontal fold reflects this point across the horizontal centre line, creating 2 holes; unfolding the vertical fold then reflects both of these across the vertical centre line, creating 4 holes in total. Each hole lies at the centre of one of the four quadrants of the original sheet, and the pattern is symmetric about both centre lines.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) A single hole at the centre would only occur if the punch were made exactly on the folded corner (the point representing the original centre) itself, not at the centre of the folded square.(B) Only 2 holes would occur if the paper had been folded only once (a single vertical fold), not twice.(D) Because the two folds are along the sheet's own axes of symmetry, unfolding always produces a symmetric pattern about the centre, never a cluster near one corner.Engineering Mathematics

Determine the nature of this critical point.(A) Local minimum(B) Local maximum(C) Saddle point(D) Cannot be determined from the given informationAnswer: (A)Explanation:First check: fx = 3x^2 - 3y, fy = 3y^2 - 3x; at (1,1), fx=0 and fy=0, confirming it is a critical point. Second derivatives: fxx = 6x = 6, fyy = 6y = 6, fxy = -3, all evaluated at (1,1). The discriminant D = fxx.fyy - (fxy)^2 = 6x6 - (-3)^2 = 36 - 9 = 27 > 0, and fxx = 6 > 0. Since D>0 and fxx>0, the point (1,1) is a local minimum.Why the other options are incorrect:(B) A local maximum would require D>0 with fxx<0, but fxx=6>0 here, ruling this out.(C) A saddle point would require D<0, but D=27>0 here, ruling this out.(D) The second-derivative (Hessian) test is conclusive here since D is nonzero (D=27), so the nature of the critical point can be determined.

questions.question: For steady-state heat conduction through a composite plane wall consisting of multiple layers in series (with different thermal conductivities and thicknesses), which of the following statements are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.B: The overall thermal resistance is the sum of the individual layer resistances
options.C: The temperature drop across each layer is directly proportional to that layer's thermal resistance
options.D: The layer with the highest thermal conductivity will have the largest temperature drop across it

(Answer in kJ/kg, to one decimal place.)Answer: 371.0 to 375.5Explanation:Sensible heat removed above freezing = 3.5 x (25 - (-2)) = 3.5 x 27 = 94.5 kJ/kg. Latent heat of fusion removed = 250 kJ/kg. Sensible heat removed below freezing = 1.8 x ((-2) - (-18)) = 1.8 x 16 = 28.8 kJ/kg. Total heat removed = 94.5 + 250 + 28.8 = 373.3 kJ/kg.
